provenance.note: Severe-injury reporting rule effective 2015-01-01. Reporting deadlines run from when the employer LEARNS of the outcome, not when it occurred. Eligibility windows: a fatality must occur within 30 days of the work-related incident; a hospitalization/amputation/loss of an eye must occur within 24 hours of the incident. Three things defeat an otherwise-reportable event: it was not actually an amputation or a qualifying hospitalization as 1904.39(b)(9)-(b)(11) define them, or it falls in one of the 1904.39(b)(3)-(b)(4) reporting exclusions. In every one of those cases the event is still RECORDABLE — only the call to OSHA drops away.
provenance.verification_note: Verified against the eCFR text of 1904.39. Rule wording here is condensed for use as a controlled vocabulary — the substance and the sub-clause cites are checked, the phrasing is not verbatim.

reporting_methods: By telephone or in person to the OSHA Area Office nearest the site of the incident (1904.39(a)(3)(i))
By telephone to the OSHA toll-free number 1-800-321-OSHA / 1-800-321-6742 (1904.39(a)(3)(ii))
By electronic submission using the reporting application at www.osha.gov (1904.39(a)(3)(iii))

in_patient_hospitalization.definition: A formal admission to the in-patient service of a hospital or clinic for CARE or TREATMENT.

excluded.rule: An in-patient hospitalization involving only OBSERVATION or DIAGNOSTIC TESTING is not reportable. Only admissions for care or treatment must be reported.

amputation.definition: The traumatic loss of a limb or other external body part.

includes.severed_or_cut_off: A part such as a limb or appendage severed, cut off, or amputated — completely or partially.
includes.fingertip_amputation: Fingertip amputations, with or without bone loss.
includes.medical_amputation: Medical amputations resulting from irreparable damage.
includes.reattached_part: Amputations of body parts that have since been reattached.

excludes.avulsion: An avulsion is not an amputation.
excludes.enucleation: An enucleation is not an amputation.
excludes.degloving: A degloving is not an amputation.
excludes.scalping: A scalping is not an amputation.
excludes.severed_ear: A severed ear is not an amputation.
excludes.broken_or_chipped_tooth: A broken or chipped tooth is not an amputation.

reporting_exclusions.note: These defeat the REPORTING obligation only. The event must still be recorded on the OSHA injury and illness records if the employer is required to keep them.

public_road_motor_vehicle_not_in_work_zo.rule: A motor vehicle accident on a public street or highway, NOT in a construction work zone, need not be reported to OSHA. If it occurred IN a construction work zone, it must be reported.

commercial_or_public_transportation.rule: An event occurring on a commercial or public transportation system — airplane, train, subway or bus — need not be reported to OSHA.

heart_attack.rule: A work-related fatality or in-patient hospitalization caused by a heart attack MUST be reported. The local OSHA Area Office director then decides whether to investigate, depending on the circumstances.

items: The location of the work-related incident
The time of the work-related incident
The type of reportable event (fatality, in-patient hospitalization, amputation, or loss of an eye)
The number of employees who suffered the event
The names of the employees who suffered the event
Your contact person and their phone number
A brief description of the work-related incident

area_office_closed.rule: If the Area Office is closed you must use either the 800 number or the online reporting application. Leaving a message on an answering machine, sending a fax, or sending an email does NOT discharge the reporting obligation.

clock_start.rule: The clock runs from the moment the event — or its work-relatedness — is reported to the employer or any of the employer's agents, whichever is the later trigger. 8 hours for a fatality; 24 hours for an in-patient hospitalization, amputation or loss of an eye.
